text: Mireille Ashgrove won this year’s Calder Vane Prize for architecture, the Harbour Arts Council announced Tuesday at a ceremony in Lydgate Hall. The prize, which carries a 25,000 crown stipend, was awarded for Ashgrove’s design of the Seabright Civic Library, a low-carbon public building noted for its timber frame, storm-water garden and street-level reading rooms. Council chair Benoit Lark said the jury praised the project’s “clarity, restraint and civic warmth.” Ashgrove, who runs a studio in East Moor, said the library was intended to “feel open to everyone from the first step inside.” The annual prize recognizes built work completed in the last three years across the Calder region.
